1.content: This chat takes place in the Warhammer Fantasy world. It is a dark fantasy setting with magic, gods, demons, and races such as Eves, Dwarves, Orcs, and others.
1.name: Overall setting

2.content:
The Empire, officially known as The Empire of Man, is the largest and most powerful of the nations of Men in the Old World.
It was founded when the king Sigmar united all the human tribes and became the first Emperor.
It is not really one centralized nation, but instead made up of 10 semiautonomous feudal Provinces, each led by an Elector Count. They are all linked by shared culture, language, religion, and loyalty to the Emperor.
The current Emperor is Karl Franz and the capital is the city of Altdorf.
2.name: The Empire of Man

3.content:
Sigmar Heldenhammer was the first Emperor, and United the human tribes to form the Empire of Man more than 2500 years ago.
He was both mighty and wise, and led mankind through many threats. In the last year of his rule, he left eastwards on an unknown quest, and never returned.
After his passing, Sigmar became the chief deity of the Empire’s Pantheon.
3.name: Sigmar

4.content:
Ghal Maraz was the name of the magical hammer given to Sigmar as a gift by the Dwarven High king. It signified the alliance between Dwarves and Humanity. It went missing after Sigmar’s disappearance, until it was rediscovered and returned to the current Emperor Karl Franz, who wields it.
The hammer is both the symbol of the Empire, and the holy icon of Sigmar worship.
4.name: Ghal Maraz

5.content:
Karl Franz is the current Emperor of The Empire of Man. He is the greatest general and statesman the Empire has seen in centuries, and it flourishes under his leadership.
He wields Sigmar’s hammer, Ghal Maraz, and has a griffon steed named Deathclaw.
5.name: Karl Franz

6.content: Reikspiel, also simply called Imperial, is the language spoken by the citizens of the Empire. It is the most widely-used tongue in the Old World. Most humans speak it, but few are educated enough to be literate. Elves, Dwarves, or other non-humans who interact with men on a regular basis also know how to speak Reikspiel.
6.name: Reikspiel

7.content:
The Grand County of Averland, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that lies in the south-east. It has the dubious honor of guarding the Black-Fire pass against regular Greenskin raids.
Averlanders are seen as slightly strange and unreliable people, but also honest and skilled at siege warfare.
7.name: Averland

8.content: The Grand Principality of Reikland is one of the founding Electoral Provinces of the Empire. It is located in the southwest region of the Empire and contains the capital, Altdorf. Its Elector Count is Emperor Karl Franz. It is considered the political, cultural, economic, and religious heartland of the Empire.
8.name: Reikland

9.content: The Grand County of Stirland, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that extends to its eastern frontier. It is a rugged highland province famous for its rural backwater society and a close affiliation with death. Their people are very superstitious due to neighboring the Vampire-controlled County of Sylvania.
9.name: Stirland

10.content: The Grand Duchy of Talabecland, is one of the founding Electoral Provinces of the Empire and is located at its geographical centre. It is maybe the largest Provence, containing most of The Great Forest, and is a thriving center of commerce and trade.
10.name: Talabecland

11.content: The Grand County of Wissenland is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that lies in the southern reaches. Wissenland is considered the armory of the Empire, for it holds the city-state of Nuln, the largest industrial city within the Old World. From its workshops and factories, Nuln churns out some of the most devastating black-powder weaponry known to Mankind.
11.name: Wissenland

12.content: The Grand Barony of Hochland, is one of the founding Electoral Provinces of the Empire. It lies in the north-central region of the Old World. Within its boundaries lies a portion of the Middle Mountains and vast tracts of untamed wilderness. Despite their backwards reputation within the Empire's more cosmopolitan regions, the people of Hochland are hardy and resourceful survivalists and hunters.
12.name: Hochland

13.content: Ostermark, officially the League of Ostermark, or sometimes called the "East March," is an Electoral Province of the Empire that was formally founded only very late in Imperial history. It lies at the far north-eastern corner of the Empire. It was always an imperial territory, but only after it’s old Capital of Mordheim was destroyed by a comet did the towns band together into the modern Ostermark. It is a fertile but hostile wilderness.
13.name: Ostermark

14.content: The Grand Barony of Nordland, is an Electoral Province of the Empire that lies on the northwestern shores of that realm. It was forced into joining the Empire in 8th century IC and has since proudly hosted the Second Imperial Fleet, protecting the Empire and merchants from sea-based threats. Raids and battles between the Nordlanders and Norscan raiders across the seas are so ingrained upon their history and culture, that none can fathom any other way of living.
14.name: Nordland

15.content: The Grand Principality of Ostland, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that makes up much of the northern border. Ostland is covered almost entirely by the dark canopy of the Forest of Shadows. The people of this land have learned to live out a rugged life among the ancient trees, clearing patches of land for their farms and settlements, and keeping a watchful eye on the murky depths of the forest.
15.name: Ostland

16.content: Middenland, officially the Grand Duchies of Middenland and Middenheim, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that lies in the north-central region. In the center of the gloomy Drakwald Forest is the capital, the fortress city-state of Middenheim, the sacred City of the White Wolf. Middenlanders are known as stubborn, proud traditionalists with short tempers.
16.name: Middenland

17.content: The Grand County of the Mootland, more commonly referred to as "The Moot," is a minor Electoral Province of the Empire that was formed in the early 11th century IC within the fertile farmlands of the south-central Old World. It is one of the main providers of food for The Empire, and is inhabited mostly by Halflings.
17.name: The Moot

18.content: The Old World is the name for the northwestern region of the world’s eastern continent. It refers to the land south of the Chaos Wastes, north of the Badlands, and east of the World’s Edge Mountains. It is the home of most human nations, as well as the Wood Elves, and many Dwarf holds.
18.name: The Old World

19.content:
Humans are the most populous race and considered the dominant species in the Mortal World. 
Most of their nations are in the Old World, but they can be found all over the world.
Humans make up the majority of the enemies of Chaos, but they’re ironically also the most susceptible to corruption, making up the majority of Chaos Warriors.
19.name: Humans

20.content: The Elves of the world long ago split into three cultures: the High Elves (Asur), the Dark Elves (Druchii), and the Wood Elves (asrai). High Elves live in the island continent of Ulthuan, Dark Elves on the northern continent Naggaroth, and Wood Elves live in the forests of the eastern continent, The Old World. Relations between the three cultures is hostile. All Elves are naturally magical.
20.name: Elves

21.content: Dwarves are a sturdy and stubborn people who once had massive city fortresses across all of The Old World, but now their holds only remain in the World’s Edge Mountains. They are a very unified people, and often trade with Mankind. Some even live as Imperial Citizens. They dislike elves, and hate greenskins and skaven. They are resistant to magic and Chaos, although some hated Dwarves betrayed their kin and joined Chaos long ago.
21.name: Dwarves

22.content:
The Orcs are the largest and most warlike of the Greenskins, and live simply to fight. They are insensitive to pain, incapable of higher thought, and bully anyone weaker than them. They are known for forming massive armies called Waaaghs to attack anyone they can find. To them, war is not only fun, but as needed as food or water.
They have green skin, red eyes, pointy ears, and a mouth full of fangs and tusks. They are massively muscular, and grow forever in size as they age.
22.name: Orcs

23.content: The Greenskins, also known as the Orc and Goblin Tribes, are a highly primitive, bestial, humanoid race of green-skinned barbarians whose sole pursuit in life is that of war and battle. The term is a common name to refer to the Orcs, Goblins, and other related subraces such as trolls snotlings and squigs. They are generally hated by most other races in the world, and they are seen as pests. Occasionally, a charismatic or mighty Orc boss can rally an army of his kind, killed a Waaagh!, rampaging across the world like a natural disaster until he is slain, or the orcs get bored and fight each other.
23.name: Greenskins

24.content:
Goblins are the smallest and perhaps the most numerous of the Greenskin race. They are, in general, a miserable and treacherous race of petty thieves and vicious cutthroats. There are many kinds all over the world, but most goblins either live in their own tribes, or in Orc tribes as servants or slaves.
They are short, green skinned, with beady red eyes and long pointed noses and ears. They are all cowardly and physically weak.
24.name: Goblins

25.content: Dark Elves are one of the most ancient, powerful, and certainly the most sadistic of the three Elven civilizations. They live in the northern continent of Naggaroth. They are raiders, slavers and heartless reavers of the highest degree, and their economy revolves entirely around slavery. They enjoy inflicting pain, and many practice Dark Magic. They hate all other races, including other types of Elves, and see themselves as superior to all.
25.name: Dark Elves

26.content: The High Elves, or the Asur, as they call themselves, are one of the most ancient and powerful mortal civilisations in the world. They live in the island continent of Ulthuan, where they consider themselves the true and rightful protectors of the world. Their culture is in decline due to their pride and hubris in their own superiority, but still they fight on against the forces of Chaos and destruction.
26.name: High Elves

27.content: Wood Elves, or Asrai in elvish, are an isolationist culture of elves who long ago abandoned their kin to live within the great forest Athel Loren in The Old World. They are highly secretive and consider themselves es the guardians of nature. They live amongst dryads and other forest spirits.
27.name: Wood Elves

28.content: The Kingdom of Bretonnia is a feudal human kingdom located west of The Old World, between the Empire of Man and the ocean. It is the second largest human nation, only surpassed by the Empire, both its greatest ally and rival. It’s culture is a feudal one that has a strict social hierarchy revolving around nobility, aristocracy, and a code of chivalry. The current Bretonnian king is Louen Leoncoeur.
28.name: Bretonnia

29.content: The Tzardom of Kislev is a human nation just north of the Empire of Man, and bordering the Chaos Wastes. It is a powerful kingdom defined by the constant need to prepare for warfare against constant Chaos-worshipping raids. They are led by a monarch called a Tzar or Tzarina. Their current Tzarina, Katarin, is known as The Ice Queen. Kislevites are a stubborn and hardy people.
29.name: Kislev

30.content: Norsca is an icy peninsula in the north that bordered the chaos wastes. The tribes that live here are mostly made up of humans, although trolls and the rare Fimir can be seen alongside them. The Norsecans, also known as Norsemen or Norse, worship the Chaos Gods. They are great warriors who often sail south on longships to raid the other civilizations.
30.name: Norscans

31.content: Sylvania is a provence East of the Empire of Man, between The Moot, Stirland, and The World’s Edge Mountains. It’s ownership is contested between the Elector Counts of Stirland, and it’s current ruler, the vampire Mannfred Von Carstein. It is a depressing, backwaters place held in the firm grip of the Vampire Counts who make up the ruling class.
31.name: Sylvania

32.content: Lizardmen are an ancient, savage, and highly intelligent race of cold-blooded, reptilian humanoids that were the first civilisation of the Known World. Alien, enigmatic, and without mercy, they follow “The Great Plan” of their creators, the Old Ones. They are led by frog-like lizardmen known as Slaan, who decipher this plan, behaving in mysterious and sometimes contradictory ways. They are sworn enemies of all Chaos corrupted races.
32.name: Lizardmen

33.content: Chaos is the term used by mortals to describe the malevolent supernatural disorder that affect the world, and anything related to it. Chaos is a force of pure, primal magic that flows from the north and south poles, where there are portals to the Realm of Chaos. This realm is a living nightmare fueled by mortal emotions, and is the home to daemonic entities that serve dark gods known as the Chaos Gods, whose only goal is to corrupt and destroy the mortal world.
33.name: Chaos

34.content: Beastmen is a loose term to refer to the many kinds of savage, mutant humanoids that bear various traits of bestial appearance, such as cloven hooves, muscular Human bodies, horned bestial heads and a primitive, malign intelligence. They are created and influenced by Chaos, and despise all civilization. They live in the twisted and dark forests of the world, as well as in the chaos wastes of the north. They periodically leave to raid, kill, rape, sacrifice, and devour other races, in groups known as brayherds.
34.name: Beastmen

35.content: The Skaven are a race of evil, intelligent, Chaos-aligned humanoid rats. The Skaven burrrow under the other civilizations, stealing their resources and plotting invasions of the surface world. They worship their own Chaos God called The Horned Rat. If they were united, the Skaven could easily dominate the entire world, but their constant backstabbing causes them to fight themselves as much as other races. Most humans don’t even know they exist.
35.name: Skaven

36.content: The Chaos Gods are divinely powerful entities that dwell in the Realm of Chaos. There are many minor gods, but the four most powerful are Slaanesh, Tzeentch, Nurgle, and Khorne. They all work against each other to increase their influence by corrupting mortals and destroying the physical world. They offer power, knowledge, and immortality to mortals that choose to serve them, but in reality they are jealous and fickle beings whose only goals are destruction.
36.name: Chaos Gods

37.content: Daemons are the malevolent entities that originate from the Realm of Chaos. They are made from raw magic and emotion, and all serve a Chaos God. Daemons can be summoned to the physical world either through dark rituals, or simply at locations dense with chaotic energy.
37.name: Daemons

38.content: The Realm of Chaos is a nightmare plane beyond the Mortal World where the evil Chaos Gods live. It is an ever-changing dimension of pure magic and emotion, where mortal dreams and fears manifest into daemonic entities. Mortal minds can hardly comprehend the full Realm, making each vision of it different. It leaks energy into the mortal world from portals at the north and south poles, fueling the Winds of Magic.
38.name: The Realm of Chaos

39.content: Khorne, also known as The Blood God or The Lord Of Skulls, is the oldest chaos god. He was created by the mortal emotions of hatred, anger, and bloodlust, and is the God of Violence, Murder and Warfare. He bestows supernatural strength and berserk bloodlust to skilled warriors, but offers no mercy for the fallen. He despises magic users as tricksters and weaklings, and forbids the use of magic amongst his followers, making him a rival of Tzeentch. He wants nothing but the world to be engulfed in endless battle, and hates anything that isn’t mindless killing, also making him the rival of Slaanesh.
39.name: Khorne

40.content: Nurgle, also known as Grandfather Nurgle or The Plague Father, is the god of disease and decay. He is fueled by mortal depression, despair and the acceptance of the cycle of life, death, decay, and rebirth. Because he embodies decay and unending cycles, he is the rival of Tzeentch. He is seen as jolly and loving, caring for each of his servants and daemons as if they were his grandchildren. His worshippers become incredibly tough and immune to pain and disease as their bodies rot with plagues and maggots. His goal is to infect the whole world with disease, watch new life grow from the rotting carcass, and then do it all again.
40.name: Nurgle

41.content: Slaanesh, also known as She Who Thirsts or The Prince of Pleasure, is the youngest Chaos God and the god of excess and lust. She can appear as either gender, both, or agender, taking the most attractive form to whoever looks upon her. Her followers perform debauched hedonistic acts in her name, constantly descending to new depths of depravity. She despises acts done without enjoyment, making her Khorne’s Rival. She offers enhanced senses, incredible wealth or beauty, and superhuman speed, but never lets her followers feel satisfied. Her goal is to plunge the world in an endless orgy of sensory indulgence.
41.name: Slaanesh

42.content: Tzeentch, the Changer of Ways, is the god of knowledge, change, and magic. He was formed of mortal ambition, hunger for knowledge, and hope for change. He is the opposite of Nurgle, and forever works to change the natural order. He weaves endless schemes for his followers to enact, often times working against his other followers or interests. He offers forbidden knowledge, powerful mutations, and magical power to his servants, but is prone to change opinions and take his favor away at any moment.
42.name: Tzeentch

43.content: The Horned Rat is a minor chaos god and patron of the Skaven. He embodies ambition, deception, ruin, hunger, deception, and self superiority. He hates all other chaos gods and plots to overthrow them all one day. He fuels the skaven’s mentality that they are better than all other life forms, including other skaven.
43.name: The Horned Rat

44.content: Hashut, The Father of Darkness, is a minor chaos god and patron of the Chaos Dwarves. He is seen as a great, flaming brass bull by his followers. He is the god of greed and tyranny, and all the malevolent things that can come from industry. He has no daemons of his own, instead giving the Chaos Dwarves the secrets of magic, industry and technology. They use these to create dominating mechanical armies, and offer Hashut an endless supply of blood, souls, and devotion in return.
44.name: Hashut

45.content:
The Winds of Magic are the eight types of magic that flow through the world. Each of these Lores has its own name, color, sources and behaviors. They invisibly ebb and flow across the world, fueling the magic of almost all races.
It is rare for humans to be sensitive to magic, and most can only master one lore their whole lives. Elves and Slaan have a natural talent, while the other races use their own forms of magic.
45.name: Winds of Magic

46.content: Azyr is the blue Wind of Magic and Lore of Heavens. It is associated with storms and celestial bodies such as stars, as is strongest within a storm. This magic is difficult to learn but highly respected. Those who can manipulate Azyr are called Blue Wizards or Astromancers, and they can change the weather and summon meteors or lightning. They can also use the art of Astromancy to read the stars and divine the future.
46.name: Azyr

47.content: Shyish is the purple Wind of Magic and the Lore of Death. Its most powerful near places of death, such as battlefields or graveyards. It allows its users to communicate with and command departed souls. Despite being mistrusted, it is not inherently evil. Amethyst wizards accept that death is part of life, and try to use this magic for good, making sure the dead remain at peace. Necromancy is a corruption of Shyish that rejects death.
47.name: Shyish

48.content: Ghyran is the green Wind of Magic and the Lore of Life. It encompasses growth, healing, curative and plant magic. It is tied to nature, and it’s strength waxes with the seasons. Green magic users are highly respected, and they are usually called Jade Wizards or Druids.
48.name: Ghyran

49.content: Ghur is the brown Wind of Magic and the Lore of Beasts. It represents the wild spirit of animals, and is strongest far from civilization. These feral magic users are called Amber Wizards or Shamans, and they live in the wild alongside animals. This magic allows them to communicate with, summon, or even transform into beasts.
49.name: Ghur

50.content: Chamon is the yellow Wind of Magic and the Lore of Metal. It is a scientific and logical magic, fueled by the mortal desire to learn. It is attracted to heavy metals such as lead or gold, and most of its spells have to do with change. It allows protection and transmutation spells, rusting metal, turning one metal into another, or hardening flesh to stone. Gold Wizards are often scientists, and they study alchemy.
50.name: Chamon

51.content: Ulgu is the Fifth Lore, the Grey Wind of Magic, and the Magic of shadows and darkness. It is the equal and opposite of light magic. It is drawn to trickery, deception, stealth as well as those who are lost and confused. It is strongest at night. Grey magic can create illusions, shadows and hide things. Users of the Imperial Grey Order are called Shadowmancers or Grey Wizards.
51.name: Ulgu

52.content: Hysh is the first lore and the white wind of light. It is the opposite of everything chaos magic represents. It is orderly and constant. It is a manifestation of light and spiritual purity. It is used for healing, abjuration and sometimes illusions. Wizards of the imperial Light Order are called White Wizards or Hierophants. Light Magic users are rare and generally peaceful, although they are sworn enemies of chaos.
52.name: Hysh

53.content: Dhar, also called Dark Magic or, more rarely, Black Magic, is a form of magic that draws on all eight of the Winds of Magic in a corrupt way. This can open one up to chaos and damage reality. It is forbidden and hated by most good people of the world. Despite this it can allow one to access more powerful magic than any other. It is used by chaos sorcerers, necromancers and other evil or irresponsible magic users.
53.name: Dhar

54.content: Aqshy is the red wind of magic and the lore of fire. It is attracted to wherever there is passion, argument, or excitement. Actual physical flame also seems to draw Aqshy. It is the most destructive magic, usually presenting as bursts of flames or explosions. It is the most likely to cause an untrained user to destroy themselves. The magic users trained and enrolled in the Empire’s Bright Order are called Bright Wizards or Pyromancers.
54.name: Aqshy

55.content: Lustria is a large, tropical continent located in the southern hemisphere of the New World and is considered to be the rightful domain of the Lizardmen race. It is located southwest of the old world, and only has been recently re-discovered by the Empire. It is known to the empire as a mysterious and dangerous land full of gold, pirates, and treasure.
55.name: Lustria

56.content: The most common kind of beastmen, they are the backbone of herd forces. They appear as mutated humanoid goats or bulls, with furry bodies, hoofed legs, and animalistic heads. While their appearance varies, They all have horns, and the larger and more impressive the horns, the higher in beastmen society the Gor is. They are all cruel and savage, and hate civilized society.
56.name: Gors

57.content: Ungors are a common beastman breed, but also the lowliest. They appear similar to satyrs, and are weaker and less intelligent than the Gor. They are low in society due to their weakness and lack of significant horns. They are relegated to forever have a life of poverty and shame, not seen as “true” beastmen by the others. Many began life as mutated human babies, abandoned by their families to die in the woods, only to survive and grow into cruel beasts.
57.name: Ungor

58.content: Centigors, or Centaurs as some call them, are a drunken, jealous race of quadrupedal humanoid savages allied with the Beastmen. They are a hybrid between four-legged animals, such as horses and oxen and bipedal beings like Humans, with a humanoid upper body with which they wield brutal weapons. Though they are not considered true Beastmen in the strictest sense, being more beast than Man, Centigors nevertheless are often seen alongside their smaller mutant brethren, especially during times of war, and to the other races, there is no difference.
58.name: Centigor

59.content: Minotaurs are a massive, bull-headed breed of Beastmen that are known for their infamously savage tempers, great size, brute strength and an insatiable hunger for hot blood and raw flesh. Often growing to twice the height of a man and far greater in muscular bulk. Though they are less intelligent than even typical Beastmen, they are unnaturally strong and powerful, and make formidable warriors. Minotaurs are possessed of a terrible hunger for flesh, particularly the flesh of Humans.
59.name: Minotaur

60.content:
A Bray-Shaman, also known as a Speaker of the Dark Council, is a powerful, if primitive, Chaos Sorcerer.
They have no need to defend themselves from other members of their tribe, because they serve as priests to the beastmen. They are gors who are skilled in magic, wielding chaos, death, shadow, and beast magic.
60.name: Bray-Shaman

61.content: Reikwald Forest Is the largest forest in the empire. Located just south outside Altdorf, it lays between the River Reik and the Grey Mountains. The main roads that link the empire to Bretonnia and the Dwarf Holds, but it is also home to many bandits, criminals, monsters, and beastmen herds. The beastmen here are particularly virile and aggressive, but thankfully still less common than common bandits.
61.name: Reikwald Forest
